title: Home

hero.lead: A quiet place to read, practise and talk. Notes on what we learn building the product, and a place to keep going.

reality.title: Current learning reality:
reality.point1: Endless feeds and surface skimming leave little lasting retention.
reality.point2: Passive consumption without practice is easily forgotten within days.

solution.title: With Noalhub, you can:
solution.point1: Read focused essays and technical notes slowly, in the open.
solution.point2: Turn reading into durable knowledge through active recall questions.
solution.point3: Keep conversations calm with people exploring the same ideas.

statement.text: Noalhub provides the bridge between reading deeply and keeping what you learn.

practice.heading: Read it once. Remember it for good.
practice.lead: After every essay, short questions bring the idea back while it is still fresh. Try three of them right here.

read.title: Read slowly
read.body: Focused essays and notes, no feed.

ask.title: Answer a few questions
ask.body: One idea per question, with the reason behind it.

keep.title: Come back to it
keep.body: Questions return as your memory fades.

q1.question: Which habit helps you remember what you read the longest?

options.o1: Re-reading the text several times in a row
options.o2: Closing the page and recalling the key idea from memory
options.o4: Reading faster to cover more pages

q2.question: You learned something today. When is the best time to review it first?

options.o2: After a day or so, just as it starts to fade
options.o3: Only the night before a test

q3.question: Why does switching between several tasks make deep reading harder?

options.o2: Each switch leaves part of your attention on the previous task
options.o3: It lowers the reading speed of the screen
options.o4: It makes the text look smaller
